mainPoints.title: The Arcade — polish pass
mainPoints.insight: Self-feeding queue — it restarts itself the moment one item ships, no prompt needed.

subtasks.text: Splatflag: fix the infinite-respawn-hit bug
subtasks.note: live 10-15 -- a downed body had no collision for 4 s. Re-checked 10-17 at the live site: still fixed.

subtasks.text: Splatflag: "a lot more colorful... a lot more to the game itself... still very incomplete"
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. You could not actually READ the game: the lines that tell you MATCH POINT, that your gun just refilled, and that you are standing in their paint and moving slow, were all pale grey on a bright yard -- the slow-paint warning scored 1.04 against 4.5 for readable, so it was invisible on the exact paint it was warning you about. They sit on dark badges now. Second: getting splatted puts you on the floor for four seconds, a quarter of the match, and the camera used to jam against whatever wall you died beside -- a flat slab over a third of a phone screen. It lifts you over the yard now so you watch the fight. Third: the big see-through circles on your screen when you get hit were literally circles, which read as smudges on glass; they are lobed paint thrown from one direction now, and they keep the middle of the screen clear. Fourth: the sky was empty -- on a phone the top quarter of every frame was flat blue with nothing in it -- so the yard has four masts and six runs of bunting strung over it in the team colours. The map itself was already fine; the roads got their pass on 10-15. Get tagged on purpose and look at what you can see.

subtasks.text: Floor-wide: bring the outline-only games up to the cartoon-outline pass
subtasks.note: Live 10-17, all twenty of them — it was twenty, not twenty-six; six had been done since the list was written. Open Out Of The Sun and look down: the city under your plane used to be a pale smear with no edges on anything, and every rooftop and street is drawn in now. Whistle Herd is second — every sheep and every stone in the wall gets a line round it. Splatflag matters too, because your own body had almost no outline at all and now it does. That one had been written off eight days ago as 'makes it worse'; the check behind that verdict compared two shots taken minutes apart of a game that never plays the same twice, so it was never a measurement. I built one that renders the same single frame both ways — old outline and new — off the same scene and the same camera, and looked at every pair. The write-off was simply wrong. Two games, Broadside Bay and Toll Bridge, turned out never to have had the brighter-on-dark pen at all, which a note last week said was finished everywhere. Costs nothing: no game draws a single extra thing. Honest limit, and it leads rather than closes: seven dark games — Fire Line worst, then Blend In, Knock On, Stand Still, Rearview, Space Golf — still have no outline you can see, and this pass could not give them one. The line we draw lands within about 8% brightness of whatever it is drawn on, so it is there and invisible. That needs you to pick a colour by eye, and it is now its own job on the list.

subtasks.text: Floor-wide: seven dark games have no cartoon outline you can see — pick the pen colour by eye
subtasks.note: Live 10-18 on four of them: Fire Line, Knock On, Blend In, Rearview. You do not need to pick a colour after all, because the colour was never really the question — I found the reason and it was an arithmetic one. The outline is drawn in a near-black plum, and the game does its brightness maths in a different scale than the one that colour was chosen in. In the scale that actually matters the plum is almost exactly as dark as a night-time floor, so the line was being drawn on top of the floor in the floor's own shade. It was always there — I built a picture of just the outline and it is a flawless line drawing, the whole cylinder, your whole body, every domino — we were painting it in invisible ink. Each of the four now uses a near-black pen chosen against its own floor, and the line you can actually see went up 4.8x on Fire Line, 2.4x on Knock On, 1.9x on Blend In. Open Fire Line: the blocks used to mush into one dark mass and now every tile has an edge. Two corrections. Stand Still does NOT have this problem — its pen already presses harder than any of the other six, and its low score is just an empty room with few things to draw, so I changed nothing there rather than fake the number. Space Golf is left: the tool that renders a game both ways will not drive it, and I will not ship a colour to a game I could not look at both ways. One thing still worth your eye: on a dark game the line can go dark (what I shipped, a cartoon outline) or bright (a rim of light). I shipped dark because that is the look the rest of the floor has. Say the word and bright is a one-line swap. UPDATE 10-18: Space Golf is done too, and live — that leaves none of the seven open. The tool would not drive it, and the reason was nothing to do with the game: it measured the picture correctly in about a second every time, then tried to hand three large screenshots back down a pipe that cannot carry that much at once, and sat there forever waiting for an answer that was never coming. Dark games squeeze down small enough to fit; Space Golf, bright and busy, does not. The pictures now go back a different way and the tool finishes in 22 seconds — on phone too, which is the bigger picture still and had never once been reached. Space Golf's line you can actually see went up 1.44x, measured three times each way because one run proves nothing. Worth knowing it was not a safe call: Space Golf is the only one of the seven with no floor, and a near-black line in a black void would simply vanish — it works because the void is not black, it is a purple nebula. Open Space Golf and look at a cluster of asteroids: it used to be one muddy brown blob and now every rock has its own edge. Hangtime measures fine now as well, but I did not touch its colour — the other worker was editing that same file at the time.

subtasks.text: Arcade lobby: fix choppy main-room movement
subtasks.note: Live 10-16. The room was giving you extra frames when you sprint or fly but NOT when you walk, so walking was the jerkiest way to move in it. Your 165 Hz screen now draws 82.5 frames a second walking instead of 55 (and a 144 Hz screen 72 instead of 48). Phones and ordinary 60 Hz laptops are untouched on purpose, and standing still still goes quiet. The 'render interpolation' guess in the title was wrong -- that was never this room's bug; the two real causes were fixed on 10-13 and 10-14 and this was the third. Walk a lap of the hall without sprinting -- that is the case that changed.

subtasks.text: Floor-wide: refresh the stale teach-cards
subtasks.note: Live 10-16. The cards themselves turned out to be right -- every game still teaches what it does. What was broken were the 40 tests that guard them: they looked for the old ALL-CAPS wording, and they gave up waiting after 3 seconds when the card deliberately holds each step up to 6 so you can read it. So those tests had been failing on every game, every run, since 10-08, and nobody could tell a real problem from the noise. Three of the five games named as 'the worst' were already fine -- the list was out of date, not the games. Fixed in 15 games, and a new check now refuses to let this rot a third time. The repaired tests immediately caught a real one: Last Call told you 'Got it' on the walking lesson without you touching the controls, because the bots shove you and it counted being thrown as walking. That one is live.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: balance the booster gates
subtasks.note: Live 10-16, and the answer was NO. The change had been shipped on 10-15 owing a test nobody ran. I ran it: 480 races across two separate sets of seeds, and giving the losing cars a bigger boost made the fastest bike win MORE -- 1 race in 4 became 1 in 3. A boost is raw speed, and raw speed is worth most to the car that is already quickest, so it widened the gap it was meant to close. The ramps pay everyone the same again. What the test found instead was bigger and is fixed too: the expensive cars could not win. Four cars costing 300-480 tickets won almost nothing in 480 races each, and the free kart beat all of them. Now the dearest three win about 15% of their races and the cheapest three about 7%. Race the Fender Flame or the Crush Toy -- both were unplayable yesterday.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: hazard-variety pass on two tracks
subtasks.note: Those two tracks already got their pass on 10-15 — four hazard zones each, live. So I did what that job left behind, and it was bigger. The house and library rooms build nine things that sit in the road on purpose — two rolling oranges, a wind-up robot, three pinball pop bumpers, two flippers and a marble — and the game had never once checked whether you hit any of them. You drove through all nine. They are solid now: the bumpers punt you sideways down the playfield (a spin in that narrow lane would just end your race), the rest bowl you over and skitter off down the road. Three of them could never have been hit even so: the oranges were aimed at the kitchen lane and sat half a metre wide of it, and the robot was walking underneath a raised, banked bit of road. All fixed and measured — the house plays no harder than before, same wreck count, two seconds slower a race. The house is the track you get first, so this is the one most people will notice.

subtasks.text: Hangtime: sound rework (verify first)
subtasks.note: Checked: the sound was already fixed and live, both notes were wrong. So I built the part of your message nobody had: dunking ON someone. The game could not tell a dunk over a man from an empty rim. Now he goes down, the screen says POSTERIZED over his name, and it is the loudest moment in the game. Live.

subtasks.text: Phone games render in a tiny box, making touch controls hard to hit
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. Thirteen games played inside a small letterboxed panel on a phone instead of using the screen. Two of them — DodgeFall and Corner Pocket — did it even holding the phone upright, where the panel was less than a third of the screen and a normal button came out 14 pixels wide. The other eleven only did it sideways, and they had been deliberately left that way since 10-08: their title screen is a tall column of big text, and on a sideways phone the PLAY button falls off the bottom of the screen, so the panel was hiding a worse problem. The old note said fixing it meant rewriting eleven games one at a time. It was one problem, not eleven: those title screens size their text off the screen's WIDTH, so a wide short screen builds a giant title. The arcade now measures any game's title card and shrinks it to fit, once a second, so it keeps working when a card changes mid-game. All 41 games on the floor were then measured on both a tall phone and a sideways one: every one now uses the whole screen with nothing cut off, and no game that already worked was touched. Four more — Splatflag, Skin Kick, Hangtime and BlendIn — turn out to have been cut off sideways all along and are fixed by the same pass. Turn the phone sideways on Convoy or Last Call: that is the case that changed most.

subtasks.text: 2v2 wagers only pay one teammate, not the whole team
subtasks.note: LIVE: Splatflag names the whole winning side and the pot splits between them; the table says so before the match

subtasks.text: A few bot-less games can never pay out, nothing scores a winner
subtasks.note:
12 of 13 fixed and live; the last one is yours to call. 10-18: Cloud Street and Broadside Bay are done and live, so 24 of the 25 games you can play with friends now name a winner. Cloud Street is a race timed to fractions of a second, and a fraction is the one thing two phones never hold the same way -- so it now ranks on the whole seconds and whole metres it already sends down the wire, and a dead heat pays both. It was worse than fractions: your own phone guesses your progress a little ahead of the host's, so EVERY race that ended on the clock would have refunded, even one you won by a kilometre. Broadside Bay is a two-ship duel with no referee -- each screen owns its own ship's sinking -- so it waits a second for the sea to settle and then reads both ships, and two ships sunk in the same volley is a draw with both stakes back. Proved with two real browsers playing each other: 18 checks on these two, 90 across all twelve, and a version that gets it wrong fails. STILL YOURS TO CALL: Hangtime, where two friends can land on the SAME team, so a two-person bet there means nothing.

EARLIER (10-17): 10 of 13 fixed and live. The 'bot-less' half did not hold up: all eight games with no bots are off the floor and have no cabinet, so nobody can reach them. What IS live is worse -- 13 of the 25 games you can play with friends said nothing at the end of a match, so if anyone bet tickets on one the pot could never be won, only handed back five minutes later. Now fixed and live: Live Wire, Haunt, Trap Doors, Comet Clash, Ice Hockey, Second Wind, Gnome Watch, Dark Room, Last Call, Last Hex. A tie splits the pot. The hard part was not the calling: the host and the people watching hold slightly different numbers, and if their two answers differ by one letter the pot refunds -- proved with two real browsers playing each other, 72 checks, and a version that gets it wrong fails. Three real bugs turned up on the way, all older than this job: Second Wind left a friend who joined a moment late watching the title screen for the whole match; it also hid the scoreboard from anyone whose connection hiccuped at the whistle; and Last Hex called the last player standing nothing at all unless that player was the host. Three games left: Cloud Street (a race, timed to fractions), Hangtime (two friends may end up on the SAME team, so a two-person bet there means nothing -- worth your call) and Broadside Bay.

subtasks.text: Space Golf: final scoreboard clips a column on phone
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. On a phone the end-of-round scoreboard cut hole 6 in half under the TOTAL column and put holes 7, 8 and 9 off the screen entirely, with nothing to tell you there was more to see — nine times '1:35.4' is simply wider than a phone. A pass last week answered it by letting the holes slide sideways, and its own check passed every single run, because it was measuring the two things that physically cannot fall off: the scrolling box, and the TOTAL column that is pinned in place. So the race is made to FIT instead. A race card does not need the clock on every hole, it needs where you lost it — each hole now shows the gap to whoever was fastest there (0 led it, +37 means 37 seconds behind), with a line under the table saying so. The whole race, all nine holes and every rival, is on one screen with no swiping. On a desktop it is unchanged, full times as before, and turning the phone mid-card can't break it. A friend with a long name used to cost you two holes; their name is shortened now instead. Checked on the live site on a phone, and the check was rewritten to measure what you can actually read — it now names the exact holes that are hidden, and is proven to go red against a copy with the fix removed.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: a camera check reports fail on every track even when nothing's wrong
subtasks.note: Done 10-17. Nothing about the game changed -- this was our own gauge lying. It claimed the camera was flinging your car 84 to 694 screen-widths off the screen on every track, including ones nobody had touched, which is not a thing that can happen. All six tracks measure 0.2 of the way to the screen edge today, so the complaint was pure instrument. It can't lie that way again: before it grades anything it checks it can see (a parked car has to appear in the middle of the frame), and a frame it genuinely cannot measure is now reported as 'cannot see' instead of being turned into a nonsense number. It also measures the thing you would actually feel -- the worst single-frame jolt of the camera -- and it is proven to still go red when the camera really is broken.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: a frame-rate check has the same blind-fail problem
subtasks.note: Done 10-17, same night as the camera gauge. The frame-rate check failed its big-screen test the same way on changed and unchanged tracks, so every run had to work out for itself that the number was noise. It now has three answers instead of two: fine, genuinely slow, or 'I could not measure this' -- the last one when every frame comes back exactly the same length, which means the machine capped the display, not that the game got heavier. Proved itself on the spot: another test browser was holding the graphics card tonight, so two of the four screen sizes came back 'cannot see' instead of crashing the run, which is what used to happen.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: old screenshots from a scrapped early build still in the folder
subtasks.note: Done 10-17. Six of them, not the five we had counted — all from the night-time city-racing build you scrapped, sitting unlabelled next to the real toy-world shots, which is how our own write-up last week picked one up thinking it was current. Moved to a folder that says what they are, with a note recording that nothing in the game reads them. Archived, not deleted. While in there I took the one thing the game's own notes called actually broken and had sat 8 days: whoever was leading took nearly every speed booster and everyone behind got a red light — the leader was taking 17 boosters for every 1 the second-placed car got. Being behind was taxed at every gate of every lap, which is why races ran away from you. The red light is now per car: the leader waits the full recharge, the back of the field waits a fraction of it. Overtaking went up and finishes got closer on both tracks tested, and no extra crashes. Live.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: a couple of outdated code comments
subtasks.note: Done and live 10-17, picked up free while the gauges were open. Two notes in the code disagreed about how long a lap is (one said 22 m, another said 60 m), so I measured all eight tracks: 18 m on the bathroom up to 60 m on the house. Three more lines still said there were six rooms when there are eight. Comments only -- nothing you can see in the game.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: friends on different wifi may still fail to connect
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. The round was agreed with two messages sent once each and never repeated: your 'I'm ready' and the host's 'we're off'. Lose either one — and on two different networks you will — and the race simply never happened: the host sat waiting on a friend who HAD hit ready, and the friend sat on a greyed-out READY button with no way out but closing the game. Both are repeated now until they land, and if the host starts without you, your button comes back instead of staying dead. The garage also told you nothing: 'Waiting for Zack' was the line whether the road was open or had never opened at all. Eight seconds of silence and it now says so by name, and tells the host it will start without them and when. Mid-race, a friend whose phone or signal dies used to leave a car sitting on the track looking alive, keeping its place and holding your results screen up to three minutes — it drops out after five seconds now, and comes straight back if their signal does, because a few seconds of nothing is usually a stutter, not a death. Proved on a test road that eats messages on purpose: four cases, all four broken before, all four fixed. One thing I could not fix from here: when two phones are on different mobile networks the connection needs a relay service we do not have an account for, and buying one is your call.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: Knockout mode is disabled in friends races
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. Knockout — last place is out every lap — was switched off the moment a friend was in the room, and if you had picked it you quietly got a different race instead, with no word either way. The reason was real: deciding who is last is a judgement, and each phone was making it for itself off its own lap counter, so two people would have been watching different races. One screen decides now — the host's, the same one that already deals the race — and it tells everyone, repeating until it lands, so a dropped message costs a fraction of a second instead of the round. Proved on two screens over a test road, including blacking the host out for three seconds on the exact moment it judged: the two screens never once named a different set of cars. The second half is that the rule now tells you first. The corner of the screen goes red and says YOU GO NEXT while you are in the cars that go when the leader comes round — before, the first you knew about it was being gone, which is a rule you cannot race against. That part is in solo races too. One thing left for you: a knocked-out friend watches the rest from the stands, and I can put them back in on the next lap instead if you would rather.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: a half-built daily event sitting unused
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. The Daily Derby was only daily in its name: sixteen cars on whatever room you were already in, a random field, open always — and a countdown that had been switched off because nothing actually happened at the hour it counted to. It is a real event now. Everybody who races it today gets the SAME sixteen cars, the same paint and the same starting slot, so two people can compare a result; it moves to a different room every day, all eight in eight days; and it rolls over at a fixed moment worldwide, which the clock in the garage counts down to honestly. Stand in the wrong room and the button tells you where today's is and takes you there in one tap, without changing your own favourite track. Your best place and time today is kept and shown with the number of goes, so running it again has a score on it. Today's is in the library.

subtasks.text: Deploy folder has a stray duplicate of the whole site sitting where a careless command could overwrite the live one
subtasks.note: Cleared 10-17. It was a whole second copy of the site -- 41 game folders, 7.3 MB -- dropped one level too high in the deploy folder on 10-04 by one mistyped command. It never went live and could never have gone live: the real site is the folder inside, and I proved it by checking that what the domain serves right now is byte-for-byte the inside one. The harm was quieter -- copying a single game into the fake copy looked like it worked and shipped nothing. Moved out to an archive folder (nothing deleted, and it can be rebuilt from scratch anyway). The deploy folder is now bare except for the real site, which is also the only proof we have of which folder the host publishes, so that bareness is now a written rule with a one-line check. Site untouched: same bytes before and after.

subtasks.text: Convoy: results screen doesn't show where your money came from
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. The end card counted points in six tiles and never once said tickets, so a round that cost a real coin finished in silence. It now carries a gold money row under the points: what you paid, which bot you beat and what that was worth, the payout for seeing the route through, and the total for the run. Every number is the server's own, so the card cannot flatter you — a run too short to pay says why, and the daily ceiling says so by name. The cause turned out not to be Convoy's at all: the arcade WAS announcing the money, but that message was painted underneath the game itself, so it has been invisible in every paying cabinet on the floor, not just this one. That is fixed for all of them at once. Play a round of Convoy and look under the score.

subtasks.text: Convoy: one mode may be paying zero tickets
subtasks.note: Checked 10-17, nothing to fix — the note behind it was out of date. All three modes pay. Measured 12 runs each against four standards of driving: easy is won 92% of the time by a good line, normal 75%, hard 33%. Hard was the worry, and it was true back on 09-30, but it was retuned on 10-04 for exactly that reason. Since 10-16 every round over 20 seconds also pays a few tickets whether you win or lose, so no mode pays nothing. One thing worth your call, not a bug: hard is an ace-only mode — a merely good line never takes it.

subtasks.text: Cliffhanger: HUD looks off on ultra-wide monitors
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. True, and not only on an ultra-wide: the game pinned every number to the corners of the glass, so on a wide monitor the height, the clock and the pitch name sat a full arm's span apart and the climb bar hugged the far edge, a metre from the climb. Nobody had ever taken a picture of this game wider than 1100 pixels. They now hold a column the width of the normal desk screen, centred on the climber, however wide the monitor gets — on your own screen it was already 1687 pixels wide and is now 1260. Phone and desk are untouched, to the pixel. Two more came out of looking at it: the big gold word that marks a moment (DYNO, SLIPPED, the pitch name) was printing straight on top of the green prompt by the next hold and on the line that tells you why a move failed — on the phone too, not just wide — so the quiet two now stand aside for the 1.3 seconds it is up; and that word was counting frames instead of seconds, so it held about half a second on your 165 Hz screen and nearly three on a slow phone. Both fixed. Play it wide and the numbers are where your eye already is.

subtasks.text: CloudStreet: two bits of HUD text overlap on phone
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. True, and worse than two bits. On a narrow phone (the common Android width, a little slimmer than yours) four players with long names folded the scoreboard onto a second row, which landed straight on the control line and clipped the climb number. Turn the phone sideways and the big shouted word sat on the control line as well, with the green LIFT arrow across it. The cause was one habit in three places: the control line, the shouted word and the LIFT arrow each had a number typed into them guessing how tall the scoreboard is, and none of them was ever right on a phone that was not yours. Nothing guesses now — the scoreboard is measured and the other three sit under whatever it actually is, and the board no longer wraps: four cards always fit one row, names shortened with a trailing dot. Checked on the live site at five screen shapes including sideways and a 320-wide phone, and I looked at the pictures. Open CloudStreet on your phone with three friends and turn it sideways.

subtasks.text: DarkRoom: multiplayer check still flaky, plus a hitch at round start
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. The two halves split apart when I measured them. The flaky one was real and worse than written down: the game asked the arcade who it was, gave up after three seconds and then ignored the answer if it came late — and a player with no room counts as the host, so a friend on a slow phone did not end up playing alone, they ended up as a SECOND host. Two separate games, each thinking the other was in it, neither thumb reaching anybody. It now takes a late answer, and a harness that is late on purpose fails on the old build and passes on this one. The hitch was not there at all: the old 'a fifth of a second every round' number came off a machine drawing with no graphics card, and on the real card — desk, a real phone, and inside the arcade itself — not one frame drops at a round start. So the slot went to the thing the blind reviewers actually complained about: a brand new player was knocked flat two seconds in, with the lesson still on step one, which is also why they thought the lesson had frozen (you cannot finish 'walk' while you are on the floor). Nobody comes for you now until the lesson is done, your first point, or thirty seconds — three of four old runs floored the learner, none of three new ones did, and the bots play exactly as hard as before. The phone picture of that first round then caught two more: the readout was saying 'they can all see you' while three bots walked straight past, and the two lines along the bottom were printing on top of each other. Both fixed. Open it on your phone and start a round.

subtasks.text: KitchenClash: whoever gets the host seat wins more than they should
subtasks.note: Live 10-17, and the answer was mostly no. I measured the kitchen itself first, with the same brain in both seats over 3,600 shifts and no network at all: neither seat wins more. The tie-break between two cooks grabbing at once already alternates, and the quick-plate crate already swaps sides every shift, so the two obvious causes were fixed before I got here. One real edge was left, and it was the person starting the game, not the rules: your friend's button had to wait its turn to be sent. The host's press counts on the very tick they press it; the guest's reached the kitchen one, two or three ticks later in a dead-even split, so on average a whole tick was handed over on every single press, before any internet delay at all. Buttons now leave the instant they are pressed -- same as the host -- and standing still costs exactly the same traffic it always did. Second thing while I was in there: on a keyboard you pressed SPACE and hoped. The phone's button has told you what it would do for months (GRAB, CHOP, COOK, SERVE), the desk never did. The bottom line now reads what SPACE does right now and what is in your hands. Play it on a laptop with a friend on a phone.

subtasks.text: TrapDoors: a results card sticks, camera crops part of the board
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. The sticking card does not happen any more -- I pressed both the start card and the end card once each, on a desk, a phone and a phone on its side, and all six cleared first press. The camera one was real and worse on a phone than anyone had written: when a tile gives way the lens dives in, and on a phone that left three tiles and one shoulder on screen -- the board gone, and three of the four people you are reading gone with it, during the one second the round actually resolves. On a desk it ate the whole near row. The reason is that every other distance this camera uses is worked out from what has to fit on screen, and the dive-in was the one number typed in by hand. It is worked out now: it holds the tile that gave way and the ring of tiles around it, so you see the hole, who went in, and where on the board it was. A third thing nobody had reported: the end card was printing straight through the last round's big shout, three layers of text in the same inch, every single match. And one more the pictures caught -- the shout was bare white letters over the board and landed exactly on the row of tile numbers, so I gave it the dark plate the NERVE readout already wears. Turning the phone sideways turned out to be a third screen nobody had ever photographed: the lesson card sat on two players' heads and the shout blanked half the board. Both fixed for that shape only. Play a round and watch what happens when a tile drops.

subtasks.text: Undercroft: camera may clip through walls, tutorial text may block the action
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. Both were real, and both were missed for the same reason: something was being treated as a point when it has a size. The camera was walked out of walls by testing the single spot the lens sits on, but a lens is a cone -- the front of it reaches about a sixth of a metre further -- so stone just that bit away was being cut open and you saw straight through the wall, while the check said the camera was clear. Over 33,000 camera frames of the crypt, the wall was cut open on 0.8% of them, and in one room 6%. The hit shake made it worse: it was added after every check had passed, up to a fifth of a metre of lens shoved sideways on exactly the blows that happen with your back to a wall, so a shaken frame clipped twice as often as a calm one. The camera now keeps a lens-sized ball of room (checked eight ways round, because a wall CORNER is reached on the diagonal), and a shake that would bury the lens is dropped for that frame -- you cannot see a shake from inside a wall anyway. Same frames after: 0.8% down to 0.4%, shaken 1.4% to 0.9%, and how often you can see the enemy is unmoved. The tutorial half was the guildmaster's lesson card: he teaches you while he swings, and the card sat where you stand. On the desk it covered your feet on all eight cards and your knees on three. On a phone held SIDEWAYS it was the bottom half of the screen -- it covered you head to feet on five cards of eight and covered him on three, while he was hitting you. The card now stands in the same column the job line and the boss bar already share, across the top, and takes the width it has: three lines wide instead of twelve lines deep. Upright phones were already clear and are untouched. Start a new character and do the yard lesson, and turn your phone sideways while he is swinging.

subtasks.text: Floor-wide: ink fix needs more games checked by eye

The cartoon outline was lifted brighter the darker the surface under it, so it ran hardest where there was least to light it -- Dark Room, a hide-in-the-dark game, was drawing its unlit room as a pale wireframe. The outline fades out with the light now and is untouched on anything lit. Only Toy Fury is left, deliberately: its file also holds booster work that is not live yet.

subtasks.note: live 10-15 -- four cards became seven

mainPoints.title: Lobby & controls — getting in and getting out
mainPoints.insight: His first item. Every exit must be impossible to miss.

subtasks.text: Lock the character until Enter is pressed — no running around the lobby before you have entered
subtasks.note: built 14:15, deploying now

subtasks.text: Escape menu button (circle with three lines) in ONE corner in every game — Hangtime has it halfway down the screen, Space Golf flips left and right
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. The button stopped moving back on the 15th — measured again today, it lands on the exact same spot in every game on both a phone and the desk. What was still wrong is that it was sitting on top of the game's own scoreboard. In Space Golf the hole's name was completely unreadable underneath it; in Hangtime on a phone it clipped the score. Both scoreboards now step aside for it, so the corner belongs to the way out and nothing else. The reason this was missed: the measurement that picked the corner looked at every game on its title screen, where no game has drawn a scoreboard yet. Looking again with the games actually running, about eighteen more have a number hidden under the button — LastHex's floor counter is completely gone, for one. Those are fixed and live too — nineteen games in all, checked on the real site on both a phone and the desk, and I looked at the pictures.

subtasks.text: Replace the small underlined "step away" / "put down the darts" links with a big red LEAVE GAME button
subtasks.note: built 14:15, deploying now

mainPoints.title: Run on a potato — smoothness deep dive
mainPoints.insight: "The main point of this game is to make it super smooth and super optimised and right now it doesn't feel like that."

subtasks.text: Flying around the lobby feels chunky and laggy — find out why and fix it
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — your 165 Hz screen now gets 82.5 frames a second while flying, and crossing into new ground builds one island a frame instead of a whole ring (138 ms to 31 ms). I also caught and fixed a bug I caused: on ordinary screens, flying was quietly making the room blurrier. Needs your eyes to confirm

subtasks.text: The shop takes a crazy long time to open — find what it is loading (aura?) and fix it
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — 2.9 s to 0.03 s. Not the aura: it was photographing all 91 skins before showing you anything

subtasks.text: Islands far away drop their props and it looks bad — find the balance between culling and looks
subtasks.note: live 10-15 — island detail switched off at 40 m but the plaza is 48 m away, so every island you could see was a bare deck. 60 m now, priced against 40/60/80: costs 5-8 draw calls

subtasks.text: Toy Fury house: make it insanely well optimized
subtasks.note: Closed 10-18, live. It holds a locked 60 fps on a phone (re-measured: 16.7 ms a frame). The loading pause was the last thing open, so I photographed it instead of guessing: on a slow phone the game showed a flat purple screen with NOTHING on it for about two seconds. The time itself is real work — building the room and drawing the first picture — and I tried the one trick that was supposed to remove it and measured that it does not, so nobody tries it again. What is fixed is that the wait now shows the game's name, which room is being set up, and a bar that keeps moving, instead of a blank rectangle.

subtasks.text: Deep dive: what it takes for the whole arcade to run on a potato
subtasks.note: 10-15 — written up with real numbers. Biggest finds: the room froze for half a second the instant it appeared (now half that, live), and our meters lie more often than the code is slow

mainPoints.title: Skins — aura rework
mainPoints.insight: Live 10-15. The outline is gone — high tiers wear fire now, and the tier is how far it has climbed you. Lighter than the old one too: the shop dresses a skin 28% faster.

subtasks.text: Aura is still choppy and does not stay with the body moving forward and back; the character leans forward
subtasks.note: The old aura slid up to 0.7 m off the body on a step. The fire is welded to you now — measured at 0.03-0.05 m walking forward and back, on the live site.

subtasks.text: Aura shows on glasses and items that should not glow — decide what actually earns aura
subtasks.note: Call made: the aura burns off YOU, not your kit. Glasses, hats, back pieces and wings are out of it. 0 of 128 flame points land on kit.

subtasks.text: The aura outline on every skin does not look the best — find a new way to give high-tier skins their aura
subtasks.note: Outline deleted. High tiers wear fire instead, and the tier is how far it has climbed you — Rare to the hips, Epic to the chest, Legendary and Divine all of you.

subtasks.text: Grand Regent: the cape clips into the body and flaps around weirdly
subtasks.note: Live. The cape sat INSIDE his back where he is widest, so the vest showed through the blue; it is now held outside his own shape, pleats fold away from him, and the hem is uneven instead of a flag.

subtasks.text: Grand Regent: the player model is broken in the shop
subtasks.note: Live. He had NO arms on the shop peg, the card thumbnail or the plaza statue — the shop draws one arm width for every skin and he is too wide, so they were buried in his chest and epaulettes. Fixed for every wide skin, not just him.

subtasks.text: Rename the godly-tier rat to "Pablo" (keep him divine)
subtasks.note: Live in the shop now — Pablo, still Divine. Only the name changed, so everyone who already owns him keeps him.

subtasks.text: Pablo: missing a neck, cheese stuck in his body — redo the whole skin
subtasks.note: Live. He had no body at all between his shoulders and his chin — you could see the floor through it. He has a neck and a scruff now. The cheese was inside his chest in every shop and card picture and inside his hip when you walked; it is in his paw, bigger, with holes. Ears are round cups so he reads as a rat from behind, and the gold crack was half buried — it shows now. Was set back to doing on a 10-17 audit because its own note still named two unbuilt parts; those were built and shipped 10-18 (paws, and a back with a shape) and it is done for real.

mainPoints.title: Lobby — center island, bridges & carpets
mainPoints.insight: "I really love the main center island." Keep every table; the connections are what look bad.

subtasks.text: Center island: keep everything (blackjack, roulette, locker), add the small details that make it look a lot better
subtasks.note: LIVE. Nothing removed. Added: a brass doorstep at each of the six exits, a pair of card-suit columns either side of the two corner exits, a red runner to all six (was four), and a velvet rope round the whole lip with gaps only at the doorways.

subtasks.text: Bridges to the outer islands land on top of the casino/roulette line — clipping; make the pathways much better
subtasks.note: LIVE. The roulette pockets and their gold frets stood higher than the carpet, so every bridge lay across them. The ring is now cut at each exit with a brass sill in the gap.

subtasks.text: The small red carpets before the jump pads clip over island props
subtasks.note: LIVE. 22 props were being covered. The carpets are now laid after the island's props exist: they thin to squeeze past one and break around one standing in the lane.

subtasks.text: Corner (diagonal) islands connect at random — give them real connecting points that read from a top view
subtasks.note: LIVE. Both corner bridges leave at exactly 45 and 135 degrees and run on that line (they were 11 and 17 degrees off, dodging a column). Each lands on a brass landing with two lamps on the island rim, and the island's own red runner carries on to its door.

subtasks.text: Check every portal: you run through it, never press E
subtasks.note: live 10-16 -- 4 of 6 doors never opened to a run; all 10 do now

subtasks.text: Inside rooms, "Exit" doors are fine where a portal does not fit
subtasks.note: the tavern and the bowling alley keep their EXIT doors; both now open to a run too

subtasks.text: Skate park: a skate-park-themed portal instead of the blue one
subtasks.note: live 10-16 -- a vert wall with a channel: quarter pipes, coping, graffiti, cones

subtasks.text: Toy Fury porch: the giant portal outside does not look good
subtasks.note: live 10-16 -- a loop of orange toy track, half the height, out on the lawn

mainPoints.title: Stardust Cavern tavern — darts & pinball
mainPoints.insight: Anything that costs a coin has to be so fun you cannot decide what to spend your coins on.

subtasks.text: Dartboard is way too big; the cabinet sides clip into the dart scoreboard
subtasks.note: Live. It was a 2 m board in a room measured in metres — now a real one, 451 mm across. The cabinet sides were only wide because the board was, so the clip into the chalkboard went with it. The throw line moved to the real distance and the view pulls in so it still aims fine on a phone.

subtasks.text: Darts: let people play against each other
subtasks.note: Live. Playing a person already worked if you were in a room with friends — but standing at the board alone it never said so, it just put you on Rusty. The panel now names who you are playing and there is a Play a friend button next to Hold to throw. Also found and fixed while looking at a phone shot: the board face was rendering as a blank brown circle from some angles.

subtasks.text: Darts is too easy — find hard-but-not-impossible; redo the whole dartboard
subtasks.note: Live. Measured it first: just holding the key averaged 104 a turn with a 180 every seventeen turns — a professional — and you could not miss the board at all. A steady hand now averages 69, a 180 is rare, holding too long throws darts off the board, and Rusty moved with you so he is still beatable if you steady.

subtasks.text: Pinball: rebuild it into a super fun pinball (2D is fine, dull is not)
subtasks.note: Live. Real recorded sound in place of the 8-bit beeps, a spinner on the right orbit that used to pay nothing, and STARDUST FRENZY — 22 seconds where the whole table pays 10x. Every ball now ends on a bonus counting up. 10-19: you said it was buggy and kind of sucked, so I measured what you actually see. The table was using 71% of a desktop screen and 58% of a phone — a small object in the middle of a room — and on a desktop the buttons sat right on the drain, hiding the one spot you watch when you lose the ball. It fills the screen now (96% desktop, 94% sideways, 72% phone), and it works turned sideways, which it did not before. On a phone: hold anywhere on the table to launch, then tap the left or right half to flip. The table also tells you the trick it never mentioned — hold a flipper to trap the ball, then shoot. That is how you aim at the ramp. And it pays now — there was no payout for pinball at all, so a game into the millions earned you nothing. A go is one coin like every other machine, and beating 500,000 pays tickets. The nightly check that was supposed to catch that turned out to be blind to the whole tavern; it isn't now, and it says the pool table and the dartboard still pay nothing.

subtasks.text: Pool balls need numbers and to actually look like pool balls
subtasks.note: Live. The striped balls had their colour band running the wrong way round the ball, so racked up they showed as a white ball with a wedge down one side. The numbers were there but the white circle was half again too big, so it covered the top of every ball like cream. Both fixed, and every ball has a shine on it now — flat colour was why they read as beads.

subtasks.text: The pool cue is half the size it should be
subtasks.note: Live. Measured: the balls on that table are deliberately a third bigger than real so you can tell a striped one apart from across the room, but the cue was left at a real cue's size. It came to 20 ball-widths long where a real cue is 26. It is 26 now, and the cue leaning on the table matches it.

subtasks.text: Jukebox: touch up the floating music notes
subtasks.note: Live. There were no music notes anywhere in the arcade — the only thing floating near a jukebox was the sparkle round the big one's star, which is probably what you saw. Real notes now rise out of both jukeboxes. The one in the bar also got rebuilt: bubble tubes down its corners and a record turning behind the glass.

subtasks.text: More detail on the bar and the pool table
subtasks.note: Live. Bar: a rack of wine glasses hanging over the counter, a tip jar, a towel over the rail, peanuts, a cut lemon, napkins. Table: brass trim round the apron, brackets at every leg, a maker's badge, leather pocket nets instead of wooden cups, two more chalk cubes and the triangle hung on the side.

mainPoints.title: Bowling island
mainPoints.insight: The main idea is good. Inside the alley is fine for now.

subtasks.text: The demo ball crashes the pins every ~5 s — loud and annoying when you stand there; find a better way
subtasks.note: It is an attract loop now: stand on the island and the lane finishes its ball, then goes quiet — full rack, ball parked, nothing moving. Only one ball in three is a strike (the rest get no cheer), the cycle is 17–23 s instead of 11, and the sound is loudest out on the carpet, not where you stand.

subtasks.text: Make the demo lane look better
subtasks.note: Pin deck with its ten spots, gutters cut as real channels with a steel lip, the neon lying in the oil, an approach with dots, a raised ball return you can watch the ball ride home on — and a sweep rake that wipes the leftover pins into the pit.

subtasks.text: The ball rack and the shoes need a lot more work
subtasks.note: The rack is a two-tier stand now (legs, shelves, chrome cradles, lit fascia, six balls with their finger holes) instead of a trough of marbles. The shoes are half again bigger on a plinth, with a real arch, a dark throat, tongue, laces and a stamped size.

mainPoints.title: Slab City — tutorial & trick progression
mainPoints.insight: A wall of controls is overwhelming. Teach the basics first, unlock tricks by levelling. A bigger park comes later.

subtasks.text: A tutorial that walks through the basics of skating, not a wall of controls
subtasks.note: Six steps, one line at a time in the panel: get on, roll, steer, push, ollie, kickflip. Each one waits until you actually do it. There is a skip.

subtasks.text: An "Open Trick Book" button showing the tricks you have learned so far
subtasks.note: The old wall of controls is shut on every device. One chip now: OPEN TRICK BOOK · LVL 1. Open, it shows a level bar, the moves you have, and the levels ahead.

subtasks.text: Levels that unlock tricks (Skate 3 style: coffin, flips as higher-level moves) and parts of the park
subtasks.note: Eight levels, ROOKIE to PRO, each opening a trick that was dead until then. The COFFIN is in at level 7 — Q with S held, lie flat and roll. I did NOT lock parts of the park, on purpose: see the report.

subtasks.text: Keep it multiplayer: skate around with others to level up
subtasks.note: XP is every combo you bank, so a session with friends levels you the same as skating alone. Two-player check green.

subtasks.text: A stray skating sound plays in the lobby — music, or a leak from the skate park? Find out
subtasks.note: Found: the skate island's little ghost board carried its wheels 26 m. Now 15 m and fading fast, and silent while you are skating.

subtasks.text: Later: grow the park once tricks and basics are in

mainPoints.title: Toy Fury — lobby island & toy house

subtasks.text: Island track: gaps at the turns; cars clip into the track and each other
subtasks.note: Each piece of road was a straight box turned onto the corner, so every joint on a turn left a third of a metre of daylight. The road is one continuous ribbon now. And the straight coming out of the loop ran right under the loop's own lower half with a foot of headroom, so cars drove through it every lap — the loop corkscrews now and the two straights are nearly three metres apart.

subtasks.text: Cars clip through the loop-de-loop and fall out of it
subtasks.note: A toy car is stiff and that loop is tight: laid flat on it, the axles sit seven centimetres under the road and the nose and tail nearly twenty. Each car now rides a touch proud of the surface by exactly that amount, only where the road curves up into it — so the flat corners are untouched.

subtasks.text: The toy decorations around the track need a lot more work
subtasks.note: Three scenes instead of scattered props: a pit lane with three numbered garages, spare shells on stands, tyre stacks and lap boards; a grandstand that went from three bears to nine on four rows under a striped canopy; and giant crayons, so you can tell the whole circuit is lying on a bedroom floor.

subtasks.text: The carpet in the main area of the house is broken and clipping
subtasks.note: Every rug was a flat box sitting at exactly the same height as the one under it, so the two fought over which one you could see — the red and yellow edges came out as a crawling stair-step. A rug laid on another sits a little higher now, the way a real one does.

subtasks.text: Clipping in almost every room — objects inside objects; build it with more intention
subtasks.note: Started with the worst one, in the room you named: the sofa was four boxes all inside each other — both arms were buried completely inside the seat cushion, and the back went 18 cm into both. It is five pieces now, each one sitting on or beside the last and none of them inside another. The cat and the cushions were re-seated to match.

subtasks.text: The mini tracks in the house should look like the real race tracks
subtasks.note: They were a flat orange noodle in one colour. Now each one is the real thing in miniature: a cream channel with the road banded in two oranges and a blue joiner every fifth piece, posts holding up the high bits, a start gantry with green lights. It costs nothing extra — the long straights are built as one piece of track instead of nine.

subtasks.text: Shrinking down into a track looks buggy
subtasks.note: Found it by filming all fourteen frames of it, which nobody had ever done. Your arms and legs never knew the body had shrunk, so a thumb-sized astronaut kept full-length limbs and folded into a blob with one arm out like a plank. The whole body shrinks together now. It also used to spin you 260 degrees on the way down, so you landed facing backwards; it turns a quarter and stops, looking down the track.

mainPoints.title: Toy Fury — race revamp
mainPoints.insight: "There's a lot of potential for this game but it just feels like I'm not even really racing."

subtasks.text: Driving: you bounce wall to wall and cannot hold the middle — make it feel like real racing, not just W + A/D
subtasks.note: The car never straightened itself: let go of a key and it kept crabbing into a wall. It eases back down the road now. Time spent scraping a rail went from a fifth of the race to one part in seventy; corners got harder to pay for it.

subtasks.text: Drop the track picker after you already chose a track (offer mode / race type instead)
subtasks.note: All eight tracks had been sitting open on the title screen permanently — the button that was meant to hide them never worked. Fixed, and once a track is chosen the race type and field are what the screen offers.

subtasks.text: Booster pads look like car-wash wipers — redesign them
subtasks.note: They were two upright brushes you drove between. Now the rollers lie across the track like treadmill drums and turn forward, with an arrow on the road.

subtasks.text: Wrecks and explosions should be a big part of it — your car can blow up and die
subtasks.note: Nothing could ever blow up before — fifteen races, zero damage. Now there is a fireball, black smoke, a shockwave that shoves whoever is near, and a car trails smoke when it is one hit from scrap.

subtasks.text: The game looks low resolution — find the cause
subtasks.note: Found it: in the arcade the game drew three quarters of the width of your screen and the shell stretched it. It draws every pixel now, at the same frame rate.

mainPoints.title: Toy Fury — car collection
mainPoints.insight: Hot Wheels: collect cars, race the cars you own, spend tickets on cars.

subtasks.text: Design many more car models — spend real time on car design
subtasks.note: Ten rides, live: a dune buggy, a pickup with a real open bed, a delivery van, a chopped hot rod with a blower through the bonnet, and a wedge with a huge wing.

subtasks.text: Collect cars and race the ones you own
subtasks.note: Buy with tickets, keep it until it breaks. The garage now says 3/10 in the garage so the collection counts.

subtasks.text: Showroom: a motorcycle is upside down; one car already has a driver in it
subtasks.note: Your own character now sits in every ride on the shelf. A wrecked bike lies on its side instead of upside down.

subtasks.text: Wheels turn weirdly and some do not attach to the car; car parts clip
subtasks.note: Turning wheels no longer tip over, the kart's front wheels are on a real axle, the bike has forks and a swingarm, and the racing stripe lies on the paint.

subtasks.text: Three cars under the win-rate floor; the ride table was only ever measured on 1 of the 8 rooms
subtasks.note: Measured all eight rooms this time, 960 races a car. The three cars named were fine once the other seven rooms counted — those numbers came from the house, which is the hardest room of the eight. The car that was actually broken was the 120-ticket Rally Pup: it won less often than the free kart, so your first purchase made you worse. It is now the quickest cheap car in a straight line and wins more than the kart. Second thing the eight-room run turned up: each car is strongest in a particular room, by a mile — the Carpet V8 wins 20 races in the garage and 1 in the bathroom. The garage card now tells you where each car wins, and stars it on the day the derby is in that room.

mainPoints.title: Multiplayer — every game
mainPoints.insight: "You're thinking of it from a very narrow lens." Think through the whole party, not one match.

subtasks.text: Pick sides: choose who is on which team
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. Sit at a team cabinet in a room and you get a SIDE A / SIDE B button, so two friends can be on the same team instead of being dealt opposite each other. It turned out not to be a job for each game at all: every one of them already works out teams from the order people sat down, so the room just hands the seats out in the order you asked for. Four cabinets so far — Splatflag, Ice Hockey, Dodgeball and Second Wind — and the button only appears where the game can actually obey it. One thing it does on its own: if you both pick the same side AND bots are off, one of you is moved across before the match starts, because a side with nobody in it is not a game. You see that happen on the button rather than finding out in the yard.

subtasks.text: Team sizes beyond 2v2 where the game allows (3v3, 4v4)
subtasks.note: Live 10-18, and "where the game allows" is doing real work here. Ice Hockey plays 3v3 AND 4v4 — the rink is wide enough for eight and both are formats real hockey plays. Splatflag and Dodgeball go to 3v3 and stop: the Splatflag courtyards are only clear for three a side, and a fourth would stand up inside a wall; the Dodgeball court is 26 across, so a fourth would be shoulder to shoulder with nowhere to dodge. Second Wind stays 2v2 on purpose — going down to become your partner's ambush needs a partner. The host picks the size at the cabinet and it is written on the board and the prompt, so nobody sits down to a different match than they agreed to.

subtasks.text: "Play again" pulls every player back in
subtasks.note: A match ends and both players get a PLAY AGAIN card instead of being dumped in the room. Pressing it sits you back at the same cabinet at the same stake, the card names who else came back, and two presses start a new match. Live, in every party game that reports its ending.

subtasks.text: The host chooses whether to fill with bots
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. BOTS or LEAVE EMPTY, next to the stake at the cabinet, host only. Left empty, the spare seats come out rather than standing there — four friends in a 3v3 play 2v2, not two people against four ghosts. The switch only shows on cabinets that can honour it, which is the point: it would otherwise have appeared on all thirty-odd party machines and changed nothing on most of them.

subtasks.text: Knocked out or finished early: spectate and choose who to watch (Toy Fury, Space Golf), never get thrown to the lobby
subtasks.note: Both games he named are live. Toy Fury: wreck or finish and the board waits — the camera cuts to a car still running, an arrow each way picks who, your result sits over it, and it ends when the last friend is done. Space Golf: hole out first and the card offers WATCH MIKE — the scorecard swaps for the chase camera on your friend, CARD puts it back, and it ends when they hole out.

subtasks.text: Bots wear skins
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. Bots in a party now wear real skins off the shop — a different one each, with its own name — instead of being team-coloured mannequins. The room deals the outfits once and sends them, so everybody's screen dresses the same bot the same way, and because they come off the live shop list, a skin you add tomorrow walks onto the floor as a bot with no game touched. A friend who leaves mid-match leaves a body behind that plays on in that seat's outfit rather than reverting to a blank. One real catch found and fixed: the shop list only loaded when somebody opened the shop, so every bot would have shipped undressed — opening a room fetches it now.

subtasks.text: Cabinets clip a lot, especially the screens
subtasks.note: Live. They were 2.5 m apart and the wide ones are 2.3 m across, so neighbours overlapped in every row. 3 m now.

subtasks.text: Clean up the cabinets; the hall is a giant box — give it a real vibe
subtasks.note: Live. Each room has its own low ceiling, carpet, a lit sign slung over every row, and posters up the walls. The old one was 7.5 m of black void over a 2 m machine.

subtasks.text: Split it: a single-player room and a multiplayer room
subtasks.note: Live. A foyer with two lit doorways: THE SOLO ROW (11 machines, cyan) and THE VERSUS FLOOR (25 with a seat for a friend, pink).

subtasks.text: The Splatflag cabinet picture still shows the old map
subtasks.note: Live. The old picture was from September, four days before the yard was rebuilt. Retaken mid-match.

subtasks.text: One room, not two — the cabinets and the five machines together
subtasks.note: Live. The games room had zero cabinets in 16 m of bare carpet; everything else was crammed next door. Now one floor: cabinets in rows down the middle, skee ball and the hoop left, the claw and the pusher right, air hockey at the end of the lit path. One wide door instead of two — on a phone you used to land facing a blank wall.

subtasks.text: Air hockey: the mallet trails your finger
subtasks.note: Live. Your mallet walked to where you pointed at 3.2 m/s — up to a third of a second behind your hand, every move. It goes where your hand is now: 12 m/s, seven frames down to two, measured on both builds with the same probe. The keys never had the problem, which is why every existing test passed on the bad version.

subtasks.text: The claw looks cheap — spheres in a row in a grey box
subtasks.note: Live. Two things: every prize was drawn facing exactly the same way on a neat grid, and the cabinet had no back, sides or roof at all — you were looking through the glass at the room behind it. The pile is tumbled now and the inside is a lit purple box. A grab still wins a prize the same way; nothing about the game changed, only what you see.

subtasks.text: Skee ball — you couldn't see past your own head
subtasks.note: Live. Your own figure stood dead centre between the camera and the lane, so you couldn't see the ball, the lane or the board. It isn't drawn while you're standing at the lane now. Raising the camera was the obvious fix and was wrong — it tilts down at the same time and pushes the board off the top of the screen.

subtasks.text: None of the five machines pays a ticket
subtasks.note: Live for the three you named. A go at air hockey, skee ball or the claw now costs one coin like every cabinet, and winning pays tickets — 8 for beating the house to seven, 4 for a plush or for rolling 300 at skee, plus the usual 3 every go pays win or lose. Signed out, you still play free and win nothing. The hoop and the coin pusher are still free and still pay nothing; I left them out on purpose rather than add a payout nothing calls.

subtasks.text: Air hockey felt dead — nothing on the table reacted
subtasks.note: Live. The mallet squashes when it strikes, harder the harder you hit; the puck stretches into a streak at speed so you can follow it; it flares as it crosses the line. Your own head was also sitting over your own goal — it steps out of shot now, same as skee ball.

subtasks.text: The hoop and the coin pusher paid nothing either
subtasks.note: Live. All five machines take a coin and pay now. Beat 24 at the hoop, or push more than 25 coins back out at the pusher. The pusher is no longer endless free play — that was a loophole once winning pays tickets.

subtasks.text: The looks still left: skee's lane, the claw's grabber
subtasks.note: Smaller leftovers, not blocking anything. Skee's lane is a flat untextured plank; the claw's grabber is a small grey blob and its chute a raw pink slab.

mainPoints.title: Coins & tickets — find the balance
mainPoints.insight: One coin a game; 100 tickets buys a skin spin. People should be able to spend pretty normally.

subtasks.text: Check daily coins actually refill (a vault note says claim_coins has never paid)

subtasks.text: "Dash in the air to reach it" did nothing, and POSTERIZED printed on top of a player's name
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. Two things the last Hangtime pass wrote down and left. The game has been telling you to dash in the air to reach a pass since the move shipped, and it bought you no extra reach at all -- only a dash along the ground did. I measured it before touching anything: a leaping player reached exactly as far as one standing still doing nothing. Now a dash in the air reaches just as far as one on the floor, and the button says PICK while you are off the ground instead of going blank. It is still something you have to DO -- jumping without kicking at the ball takes nothing, which I checked, and the computer players don't use it, so the move is yours and the game plays the same otherwise. Second: on a wide screen, when you dunked on someone, the big red POSTERIZED landed directly on top of YOUR OWN floating name -- a grey tag with half its letters poking out of the word. Names under the banner now fade out of the way for the two seconds it is up. An upright phone was never affected, and I left it alone there. subtasks.text: Cold load shows a black "Loading the arcade..." card for several seconds, worse on a slow/throttled phone
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. Measured on your real site on a slow phone first: eleven seconds of a card with not one moving pixel, so there was no way to tell a loading arcade from a hung one. Three things were wrong underneath. The arcade was waiting its turn for no reason -- the page finished arriving before the browser even thought to go and fetch the 3D library, so the two queued up instead of coming together; they now come together, and on a phone with decent signal you are in the room in under five seconds. A white "Play from a plain list instead" button was being shown to every single visitor from the first moment, as if the arcade had failed -- it was meant to appear only on a failure and had never worked, because of a rule this file had already patched thirty-five times in other places and never once here. And the card's own timers were counting from the wrong moment: they sat at the very bottom of a very large page, so they started when the browser finished reading, not when you arrived -- a "twelve second" rescue was firing at twenty-two. The card now has a sweeping bar and tells you where it has got to (loading, then building the room, then warming up the lights), the way out is offered after six seconds if you are genuinely waiting, and the "it did not load" message can no longer cry wolf on a load that is merely slow. Open the site cold on your phone and watch the card.

subtasks.text: favicon.ico 404s every session -- the one console error a stranger's browser logs
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. A yellow B on plum, in the site's own colours. One small file at the root rather than an edit to every page, because browsers ask for it whether a page mentions it or not -- so the error is gone from the arcade, the games list, About, the not-found page and all 62 game pages at once. A cold visit to the live site now logs no bad responses at all, where before it logged exactly this one.

subtasks.text: Guest economy messaging contradicts itself: coins "refill on their own", the purse count is hidden on the floor, every cabinet charges 3 coins, and a guest with 0 still gets to play
subtasks.note: Live 10-17. One story now, told at the cashier: tap your purse and a card explains coins, tickets and skins in three lines, with every number read from the database. The tour had said two coins an hour for nine days while the server paid ten. A guest keeps a pill reading 'Guest - nothing saved' instead of nothing at all, and is let into every cabinet -- eight used to refuse them. A go is 1 coin, not 3; a guest is quoted Free, because that is what they pay.

subtasks.text: Cabinet "Play" prompt clips the price text on a 390px phone ("Broadside Bay . 3 c...")
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. It was 27 of 29 signs on the floor, not just this one, and only on an upright phone. All 29 read in full now -- the line takes a second row and never splits '3 coins'.

subtasks.text: The shop sits 44m behind spawn, off-screen from the hall -- easy for a guest to never find
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. Measured first: there were exactly two shop stands in the whole arcade and both were on the plaza, so the big arcade -- where you earn every ticket you own and where you spend the whole visit -- had none. The plaza centrepiece stays put; the shop came to you. The big arcade's prize counter was scenery under a sign promising soft toys nobody could buy, and it is a real stand now: walk up, press E, same shop, 98 skins and the 100-ticket case. It also moved, off the side wall and onto the lane between where you land and the way out, because on a 390px phone anything off to the side is simply gone. Walking out of the solo room the shop is in view 19 of 22 frames and the prompt comes up on its own; out of the versus room, 16 of 22. Checked on the live site, desk and phone.

subtasks.text: Hangtime: on a 390px phone the slam's blast-dome effect covers most of the court
subtasks.note: It was a ring 45% as thick as it was wide, which at eight metres across and turned flat to the camera is not a ring, it is a disc -- and the screen flash was brightest exactly where the rim is. The explosion was covering the dunk it was advertising. It is a thin shockwave now that sweeps out past the frame, and the flash blows the edges and leaves the middle alone. Shot both builds at the same frame of the same staged dunk to compare: before, a solid pink disc over rim, dunker and victim; after, you can see all three. Live.

subtasks.text: Hangtime: the "pick" (intercepting a pass) mechanic is inert -- fires 0.1/game, no bot or button ever uses it
subtasks.note: It had a banner, a screen shake and a line reading 'you jumped the lane', and no way to jump a lane: a pass crosses at 16 m/s against a grab radius of two feet, so the whole window was a tenth of a second of standing in the right spot. The dash is the act now -- with no ball in your hands, a dash at a ball in the air reaches for it, and the button says PICK while the throw is live. Proved it is a verb and not just a wider net: same pass, same frames, standing still takes it 0 times and a dash takes it every time. 0.1 a game to 1.0 a game, and 24% of passes -- which is the number this game has claimed in its own comments since September and never once delivered. Live.

subtasks.text: Hangtime: whether the 120ms dash-to-dunk timing window is fair needs an A/B -- not yet tested on real players
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. A/B'd at last, and it was not fair -- not because it was hard, but because it was a computer-only move. On a phone the DASH and SHOOT buttons are 105 pixels apart and one thumb has to cover both, which takes about a quarter of a second; the window shut before that. Over 400 attempts where the player did everything right, it paid the three to 81 in 100 on a computer and 11 in 100 on a phone. The button lied on top of it: it stopped saying MOON DUNK about a fifth of a second before the jump stopped being worth three, so the one thing telling you the move exists went dark while your thumb was still travelling. The payout, the button, the on-court ring and the hint were four separate copies of the same rule and they disagreed. One rule now, held open long enough for a thumb: 11 in 100 becomes 86 in 100 on a phone, 100 in 100 on a computer. Deliberately not opened wider than that -- going further starts paying three for a layup. Bot play is unchanged, proved line-for-line against the old build on 120 games, with a deliberately-broken copy run first to show the test can actually see this setting.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: muscle, van and monster cars still sit just under the 6% win-rate floor; 7 of 8 tracks' ride table was never measured
subtasks.note: Answered 10-18, and the complaint was wrong. The old numbers came from one room, and the house is the harshest of the eight. Raced over all eight rooms, 480 races per car: muscle wins 16.7% of the time, monster 10.4%, van 7.5% — all three well clear. The car that really was too weak was the 120-ticket Rally Pup, the first car you can buy: it won LESS than the free kart, so your first purchase made you worse. It is quicker now and live. subtasks.text: Skin audit: 20 fixes found across 60 skins (dark legs on dark floor x7, planks seen edge-on x7, tilted attachments x4, a part over the face x4) -- worst class first, not yet started
subtasks.note: Checked all 60 by machine instead of by eye, and 19 of the 20 were already fixed. The 'dark legs on a dark floor' worry is backwards: the dark floor is the SAFEST place to stand, because the room lights your legs wherever you are. Measured every character on four different floors -- 78 of 91 never lose their legs anywhere, and the worst loses a quarter of one and still looks fine, so no colour needed changing. One fix was real and is now live: the Samurai has never had eyes at all, and now does.

subtasks.text: Toy Fury: rivals play weaker when you are watching, so the in-game teach card may show an easier version than the real difficulty
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. The rivals do not ease off: I ran the same race twice, once with the picture drawing and once with nothing on screen, and every one of the eight cars finished on the same millimetre. Nothing in the game asks whether anyone is looking, and the teach card never touches the difficulty. But chasing it turned up something worse that nobody had reported. Three of the eight rooms had a corner no car in the game can take -- the garage, the library and the classroom -- a bend tighter than the road is wide, right before the finish line. You lost a panel there on every single lap, so you lost the car itself three laps in, and a car is gone for good and costs tickets. Measured: on the EASIEST setting your car was wrecked 22 races in 112, and in the garage and the library it was every race, 8 out of 8. All three corners are re-laid as real curves -- still the hardest corner in their room, now ones a car can actually get round. Same test now: wrecked 5 races in 112, and two and a half cars finish a race where barely one did. It fixed the difficulty buttons as a side effect: ROOKIE, RACER and CHAMPION used to put the same driver in 4.6th, 5.0th and 4.9th place -- the hardest setting was the easy one -- and now read 2.8th, 4.1st and 5.6th, with 23 wins, 10 and 1. Still owed, and it is older than this: the moto and the wedge cannot finish the garage or the classroom at all.

subtasks.text: Pablo skin: body is one smooth mass with no paws
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. He has four pink paws with toes now, and furry arms down to them -- before, his hands and feet were the plain cream balls every character starts with. His back has a shape: two haunches over his back legs with the gold crack running down the groove between them, where before it was one smooth slope from his neck to his tail. His pale chest is finally visible -- it was being drawn 2.5 mm in front of his fur, so the two were fighting over the same pixels and you saw neither. The cheese is smaller and sits in the paw instead of floating beside it: it had been sized against an empty hand, so it was two and a half times bigger than the hand holding it. One catch worth knowing: the paws only show on YOUR rat as you walk around -- the shop picture, the card and the statue draw simpler hands, so those now show the right colour but not the toes.

subtasks.text: Undercroft: two pillars in floor 1's hall sit 0.78m apart and against the wall, pocketing a player -- no minimum pillar spacing
subtasks.note: Obsolete on re-check, 10-17. Measured all six contracts: zero slots a player fits through that a melee foe does not. Your body is 0.72m across and every melee foe is wider (skeleton 0.84, warden 0.96, brute 1.20), so that 0.72-0.84m band is the thing that matters and nothing is in it. The narrowest walkable slot anywhere is 0.881m, fixed guild-hall geometry, and a skeleton still fits. The old coordinates are not even in today's map. The row also inverted its source -- the original note says a person walks round it; it was a test robot that stalled. Shipped the missing spacing rule as a check that plants the old defect every run and must find it before it trusts a zero.

subtasks.text: Undercroft: the Blade enemy is near-unbeatable for an average player (0/24) vs a good one (16/24), never tuned
subtasks.note: Obsolete on re-check, 10-17. The Blade was never an enemy -- it was one of two player kits, and that whole system was replaced by the five classes. Its descendant is the rogue. The harness that produced 0-of-24 cannot even attach to today's game any more. A gap of about 2x against the knight survives on one seed, which is one sample and not enough to retune a class everyone plays -- a pooled run is queued.

Toy Fury: friends on different mobile networks may still fail to connect without a TURN relay
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. The premise was wrong in a useful way: they DO connect. When the direct phone-to-phone link cannot cross two mobile networks, the arcade already falls back to the backup server, which carries everything a relay would and more. Nobody had asked what the race looks like after that, and the answer was bad -- the backup server sends in bursts every couple of seconds, and between bursts your friend's car stopped dead and then teleported. Measured: it stood still for 82% of the race and was drawn 26 car lengths from where it really was. Now their car keeps driving down the track at its last speed until the next burst arrives: still 0% of the time, and 9 car lengths out. Second thing, same failure: if the road never opens at all, the guest used to be stuck in the garage with a greyed-out button forever. There is now a RACE ALONE button and a line telling them to try the same wifi. Still no paid relay account and none needed for this.

subtasks.text: Hangtime: confirm the POSTERIZED call fires correctly for a man genuinely under the rim, now that the radius is 1.4
subtasks.note: Confirmed, and the answer was no. Measured over 400 games and 1026 dunks: of the men it named, 59% were further from the dunker than the radius allows by the time the word printed, 29% were behind the backboard, and the worst was nearly four metres away. No radius could have fixed it -- the game picked the victim early in the flight and the man then had most of a second to coast past the rim with nothing steering him, so the rule and the picture were taken at different moments. The word is decided at the rim now, from where everyone actually is. Same 400 games either side: it still fires as often (0.20 a game against 0.21) and the worst case fell from 3.85 m to 2.24 m. Live.

subtasks.text: Shop: the statue showing a random skin sometimes disappears (queue 91)
subtasks.note: Live 10-18. Walking far enough away from the plaza unloads it, and when you walked back the room was rebuilt but nobody put the figure back — so you came home to an empty lit plinth until the skin changed on its own, up to twenty minutes later. It is dressed the moment the room comes back now. subtasks.text: Music: deep dive, more tracks per spot, randomized (queue 92)
subtasks.note: Live. 37 more songs, all free to use, so every spot has a deeper pool: the plaza and the big arcade hall went from 3 songs to 7, the tavern, bowling, skate park and toy house from 3 to 6, the crypt gate 2 to 5, the Undercroft guild hall 4 to 7. 100 songs in all. The shuffle was already there and was never the problem -- three songs was. subtasks.text: Bowling: pins clip into the floor, rolling sound, pins glitchy from above (queue 93, repeat of 29)
subtasks.note: All three, and I measured each one on the live site before touching anything. The pins sank because a fallen pin was lifted 55 mm and a pin is 60 mm thick, on a deck 13 mm up — so every pin that went down lay 18 mm inside the wood with its belly sliced flat. They rest on it now. A pin knocked backwards used to drop 30 cm straight through the lane in one frame; only pins that reach the pit fall, and they fall properly. The glitchy look was the two red stripes: they were being smeared into one soft blob half the pin deep, worst on the island where the pins are four times life size. They are two crisp stripes again, and the giant pin on the sign — which had no stripes at all — has them. The roll was one flat drone at one pitch that cut off dead just before the crash; it follows the ball's speed now and fades into the crash. Live.
